content: Side Effects: Common side effects of this medication may include headache, nausea, vomiting, joint pain, diarrhea, abdominal pain, fever, sore throat, difficulty sleeping, or loss of appetite. It is important to remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits to you outweigh the potential risks of side effects. In rare cases, balsalazide may exacerbate ulcerative colitis. Severe allergic reactions to this medication are extremely rare. This is not an exhaustive list of possible side effects. If you are in the United States, contact your doctor for medical advice regarding side effects. If you are in Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Precautions: Before starting balsalazide, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to other aminosalicylates (such as mesalamine or olsalazine), to salicylates (such as aspirin or salsalate), to sulfasalazine, or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could trigger allergic reactions or other problems. This medication may increase your sensitivity to sunlight, particularly if you have pre-existing skin conditions such as atopic dermatitis or eczema. Limit your time in the sun, avoid tanning booths and sunlamps, and use sunscreen and protective clothing when outdoors. This medication contains sodium and is chemically similar to aspirin. Children and teenagers under 18 years of age should not take aspirin if they have chickenpox, the flu, an undiagnosed illness, or have recently received a vaccine. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary. It may pass into breast milk, so consult your doctor if you are breastfeeding. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions can alter how your medications work or increase your risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal supplements, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Balsalazide is very similar to mesalamine. This medication may interfere with certain laboratory tests, such as urine normetanephrine levels, potentially leading to false test results. Overdose: If someone has overdosed and is experiencing severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. In the United States, you can call 1-800-222-1222. Lab Tests and Monitoring: While taking this medication, your doctor may order laboratory tests, such as kidney and liver function tests, to monitor your health. Be sure to attend all medical and laboratory appointments as scheduled. Missed Dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is close to the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Do not double the dose to catch up. Storage: Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Important Information: This document provides a summary and does not contain all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that this product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for individual medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
